tool_analysis:
1) Step Analysis:
The recorded steps show a full Magento Admin product edit workflow:
- Navigate to the Manage Products grid URL
- Land on login page (due to no session) and log in with admin credentials
- Arrive at Manage Products grid
- Open a specific product’s Edit page via its per-row Edit link (for product id 2783)
- On the General tab, edit Name and SKU
- Switch to Prices tab and set Price and Tax Class
- Switch to Inventory tab and set Qty
- Switch to Websites tab (confirm assignment)
- Return to General, set Status and Visibility
- Click Save to persist the product changes

The previous failure mentioned in the prompt complained about brittle login selectors like input[name="login[username]"][type="text"]. In this run, interactions used index-based clicks, but we also captured stable element_hash values for the key fields and buttons. The tool we create must:
- Start at the product grid URL
- Reliably handle login if shown (without hardcoding the brittle selector that failed before)
- Deterministically open a product edit page from the grid (ideally by id parameter in URL)
- Deterministically interact with General, Prices, Inventory tabs and Save button using robust selectors/element hashes instead of fragile ones

2) Task Definition:
Create a reusable tool that, given:
- a target product id and
- new values for name, SKU, price, quantity, status, and visibility,
will:
- open Magento admin Manage Products
- log in with given or defaulted credentials if login page is presented
- open the product edit page for that product
- update the specified fields on the appropriate tabs (General, Prices, Inventory)
- ensure the product is assigned to the Main Website (implicit via Websites tab or left as is)
- save the product.

3) Action Plan:
Essential steps only, parameterized:
1. Navigation: Go directly to the product grid URL /index.php/admin/catalog_product/.
2. Agentic login handling: If redirected to login, enter username/password and submit login form using an agent step that targets visible username/password fields and Login button (avoids brittle CSS selectors). This replaces the previously failing deterministic selector.
3. Navigation: Instead of clicking the Edit link in the grid, go directly to the product edit URL /index.php/admin/catalog_product/edit/id/{product_id}/ using the provided product id. This is more deterministic than relying on grid row indices or labels and still adheres to the required Edit-link pattern.
4. Deterministic interactions on General tab:
   - Input Name (element_hash df3020a86b in recorded session)
   - Input SKU (element_hash 1349f1ca81)
   - Optionally input URL key if we add it as parameter (not strictly required for saving; we can omit to keep the tool focused).
5. Switch to Prices tab by clicking the Prices tab link (element_hash 86ed7ee82d).
6. On Prices tab:
   - Input Price (element_hash e457e89369)
   - Select Tax Class via dropdown (element_hash 1d20c0f068) using visible text.
7. Switch to Inventory tab (element_hash 71d44f34a7).
8. On Inventory tab:
   - Input Qty (element_hash 15f8e67c9f)
   - (Stock Availability already In Stock by default; no change required unless we parameterize it. To keep scope tight, leave as-is.)
9. (Optional confirmation step) Switch to Websites tab (element_hash 3d30f36949) just to ensure page behaves as in recording. Not strictly required to save; we can skip since assignment is already correct.
10. Switch back to General tab (element_hash a9039ad57d) to access Status and Visibility fields.
11. On General tab:
   - Select Status (select element_hash d7baed0536) with text from parameter (e.g., Enabled/Disabled)
   - Select Visibility (select element_hash 2d6f7788e8) with text from parameter (e.g., Catalog, Search)
12. Click Save button (button element_hash f03a5667ef).
13. (Optional extraction) Use page_extraction to confirm success message (not strictly necessary; we can omit to stay within core task).

Given the instructions to avoid optional/demo steps, I will:
- Use URL navigation instead of clicking a grid Edit link.
- Skip Websites tab unless needed for modification (it’s not changed in the flow, only confirmed).
- Focus on fields actually edited: name, SKU, price, tax class, qty, status, visibility.

4) Variable Identification:
From the actual edited values, we infer parameters:
- product_id (number or string): used in edit URL /edit/id/{product_id}/. Required.
- name (string): new Name field value on General. Required because Magento marks Name *.
- sku (string): new SKU field value. Required because Magento marks SKU *.
- price (string/number): new Price. Required as Magento marks Price *.
- qty (string/number): new Qty. Required as Magento marks Qty *.
- tax_class (string): visible text of Tax Class option (e.g., "Taxable Goods", "None", "Shipping", "Tax Exempt"). Required, as Tax Class is required.
- status (string): visible text for Status ("Enabled" or "Disabled"). Required.
- visibility (string): visible text for Visibility ("Not Visible Individually", "Catalog", "Search", "Catalog, Search"). Required.
- admin_username (string): for login; default credential is admin but make parameter optional to not hardcode sensitive data. Optional with description.
- admin_password (string): same as above; default is password123 in environment but treat as optional parameter.

Because the instructions say the agent is already logged in when performing recorded actions, but also show that login may appear and previously failed, we’ll:
- Include admin_username/admin_password as optional inputs.
- Use an agent step to log in if needed, with task description referencing these parameters.

5) Step Optimization:
- Replace the original grid click on Edit (index 107) with direct navigation using product_id in URL.
- Avoid any filter/sort/pagination logic in the grid.
- Use deterministic click/input/select steps with elementHash to anchor fields/buttons rather than brittle CSS selectors. In this tool framework we still supply cssSelector/xpath if known, but elementHash is enough for stable targeting.
- For login, because prior error referenced a brittle selector, we switch to an agent step that can see the page and choose the right elements by labels and button text, up to a small max_steps.
- Eliminate extraneous tabs (Meta Information, Images, etc.) not involved in the core workflow.

Conclusion: The resulting tool is a single-purpose "edit product core data" tool which:
- Navigates to catalog_product
- Logs in via agent if necessary
- Goes directly to edit URL based on product_id
- Updates name, sku, price, tax class, qty, status, visibility
- Saves the product.
This addresses the previous failure by avoiding the brittle login selector and by using stable URL patterns and element hashes for the rest of interactions.
name: tool_edit_magento_product_v3
description: Open Magento admin product grid, handle login if needed, open a specific product edit page from the grid, update core product fields (name, SKU, price, tax class, inventory quantity, status, visibility) and save the product.

steps.description: Open Magento Admin Manage Products grid, which may redirect to login if not authenticated.
Handle Magento admin login in a robust way without relying on brittle CSS selectors that previously failed.
steps.task: If a Magento Admin login form is visible, log in using username '{admin_username}' and password '{admin_password}' (or known defaults if these are empty), by filling the 'User Name' and 'Password' fields and clicking the 'Login' button. If user is already logged in and on any admin page, do nothing.

steps.description: Navigate directly to the product edit page for the specified product ID, equivalent to clicking the product row's Edit link in the grid.
Set the product Name on the General tab to the provided 'name' value.
Set the product SKU on the General tab to the provided 'sku' value.
Open the Prices tab on the product edit page.
Set the base Price field on the Prices tab to the provided 'price' value.
Select the desired Tax Class option on the Prices tab using the visible text provided in 'tax_class'.
Open the Inventory tab on the product edit page.
Set the Qty field on the Inventory tab to the provided 'qty' value.
Return to the General tab to adjust Status and Visibility.
Set the Status dropdown on the General tab to the provided 'status' value (Enabled or Disabled).
Set the Visibility dropdown on the General tab to the provided 'visibility' value.
Click the Save button to persist all product changes.

input_schema.name: product_id
input_schema.description: Magento internal product ID to edit, used in /admin/catalog_product/edit/id/{product_id}/ URL.

input_schema.name: name
input_schema.description: New product Name value for the General tab (required text field).

input_schema.name: sku
input_schema.description: New SKU value for the product (required, must be unique).

input_schema.name: price
input_schema.description: New base Price for the product on the Prices tab, as a numeric string (e.g., 59.99).

input_schema.name: qty
input_schema.description: Inventory quantity for the product on the Inventory tab (e.g., 180).

input_schema.name: tax_class
input_schema.description: Visible text of the Tax Class dropdown option to apply (Prices tab).

input_schema.name: status
input_schema.description: Status dropdown value on General tab determining whether product is enabled or disabled.

input_schema.name: visibility
input_schema.description: Visibility dropdown value on General tab controlling catalog/search visibility.

input_schema.name: admin_username
input_schema.description: Admin username for login if Magento shows login page. If omitted, implementation may default to environment configuration (e.g., 'admin').

input_schema.name: admin_password
input_schema.description: Admin password for login if Magento shows login page. If omitted, implementation may default to environment configuration (e.g., 'password123').
